signals.entity: Bank of Cyprus Public Company Ltd + JCC Payment Systems Ltd
signals.signal: Both selected by the ECB among 36 payment service providers euro-area-wide for the digital-euro PILOT phase (ECB press release 14/07/2026; call for expressions of interest March 2026, >50 applicants, outcomes notified end-June 2026). Pilot starts H2-2027 and runs 12 months; it covers person-to-person and person-to-business payments on a beta digital euro in a controlled environment, and requires each PSP to build pilot payment services, onboard/integrate to the digital-euro service platform, run user testing and back-end certification. The Central Bank of Cyprus said it will work closely with both. First time Cyprus appears in the digital-euro delivery chain. ('Digital euro' = a central-bank-issued electronic form of cash that banks and PSPs would distribute through their own apps and terminals.)
signals.source_name: European Central Bank - press release 'ECB selects 36 payment service providers to join digital euro pilot' (regulator) + Cyprus Mail 14/07/2026
signals.implies: Digital-euro acceptance has to land on physical and self-service rails: POS terminals and acquiring/TMS (JCC), ATMs and self-service kiosks for load/unload of digital euro (Bank of Cyprus, 132 ATMs), plus HSM/key management and onboarding. Printec entry points: Verifone/Castles terminals + TMS software updates for digital-euro acceptance, softPOS, NCR/x-core ATM software changes for digital-euro funding/defunding at ATMs, Thales HSM and remote key injection, eKYC for pilot user onboarding, and managed services for the terminal-estate rollout. Build work starts 2026-2027, i.e. procurement decisions inside the next 12-18 months.
signals.likelihood: High - PSP participation agreements being signed now, build phase precedes H2-2027
signals.followup: Approach Bank of Cyprus and JCC digital-euro programme owners in Q4-2026 on ATM and POS acceptance rails; check the ECB pilot page for the full named participant list and any published technical scheme rulebook requirements for terminals.

signals.entity: Association of Cyprus Banks / all Cypriot banks + JCC + DIAS (Greece)
signals.signal: A shared, optional inter-bank MOBILE payment platform is under development for Cyprus that would let customers of participating banks send instant payments using a mobile phone number or e-mail address instead of an IBAN - built in cooperation with JCC and the Greek interbank operator DIAS (the operator behind Greece's IRIS scheme). Cypriot banks were 'exploring technical feasibility', with launch possible 'sometime in 2026' if development proceeds; the full-participation timetable is not yet clarified. Context: instant-payment obligations already bit under the EU Instant Payments Regulation - receive from 09/01/2025, send from 09/10/2025, Verification of Payee (checking the beneficiary name matches the IBAN before a transfer is confirmed) from October 2025, and fee parity with standard transfers from 09/01/2025. Base source ACB 08/10/2025 / Politis 09/10/2025 - retained because the launch trigger falls inside the next 18 months.
signals.source_name: Association of Cyprus Banks - 'Pliris efarmogi ton Ameson Pliromon stin Kypro' (industry body, primary) + Politis 'Cyprus Banking in the Era of Instant Payments'
signals.implies: A DIAS-built IBAN-less P2P scheme in Cyprus mirrors Greek IRIS - and in Greece IRIS moved from P2P into POS acceptance, which is where the terminal estate has to change. Printec entry points: POS terminals and terminal management (TMS) for eventual IRIS-style POS acceptance in Cyprus, softPOS for micro-merchants, ISO 20022/instant-payments integration work, and INETCO transaction monitoring for a new real-time rail. Printec already has the Greek IRIS/DIAS/EuroPA context from the 2026-07-24 Greece run - directly transferable.
signals.likelihood: Medium - launch slipping; no confirmed go-live date as of 31/07/2026
signals.followup: Ask DIAS (existing Greek relationship) and JCC whether the Cyprus mobile-payments scheme includes a POS-acceptance phase, and when; watch centralbank.cy and acb.com.cy for a launch announcement.

signals.entity: Central Bank of Cyprus / Cyprus payments market
signals.signal: CBC payment statistics for H2-2025, published/reported 22/07/2026: non-cash payments +8% in volume to 174 million transactions and +9% in value to EUR 148bn (vs euro-area +7%); CARD payments are 75% of all non-cash transactions by volume - the HIGHEST share in the euro area, against a 57% euro-area average; over 73% of domestic ATMs support CONTACTLESS, versus a 38% euro-area average; instant transfers reached almost 32% of SEPA credit transfers by volume; cheques still carry 6% of total payment value at an average EUR 4,000 per cheque (euro-area average EUR 1,200).
signals.source_name: Cyprus Mail reporting Central Bank of Cyprus H2-2025 payment statistics
signals.implies: Two concrete openings. (1) 73% ATM contactless penetration means ~27% of the 321-ATM national estate still lacks contactless - a defined hardware/software refresh target for NCR ATMs and x-core. (2) Cheques at 6% of value and EUR 4,000 average keep BUSINESS cheque-deposit and coin/banknote machines alive in Cyprus longer than elsewhere - a live case for intelligent-deposit/recycling ATMs and Glory/Sesami cash automation rather than pure withdrawal ATMs. Card dominance at 75% also underpins POS/acquiring, TMS and softPOS demand.
signals.likelihood: High - published regulator data, refresh decisions annual
signals.followup: Pull the underlying CBC payment-statistics release from centralbank.cy for the per-bank ATM contactless split, and use the ~27% non-contactless ATM gap as the opening pitch to Bank of Cyprus and Eurobank Limited.

signals.entity: Cyprus banking sector (Association of Cyprus Banks members)
signals.signal: Sector estate sizing from ACB annual-report data, published 02/07/2026: 8 member banks (from 12 in 2013), 6,253 employees (-33% vs 2013), 155 branches (-60%), 321 ATMs (-24% from 423). Per bank in 2026 - Eurobank Limited 59 branches / 156 ATMs / 2,450 staff; Bank of Cyprus 56 / 132 / 2,447; Alpha Bank Cyprus 25 / 26 / 746; NBG (Cyprus) 2 / 4 / 143; Societe Generale Bank Cyprus 3 / 3 / 113; Housing Finance Corporation 5 / 0 / 83; Ancoria 3 / 0 / 138; cdbbank 2 / 0 / 133.
signals.source_name: CBN (Cyprus Business News), citing Association of Cyprus Banks annual reports
signals.implies: The addressable ATM/self-service market in Cyprus is effectively two accounts - Eurobank Limited (156) and Bank of Cyprus (132) = 90% of the national estate - with Alpha Bank Cyprus (26) a distant third. Branch count falling far faster than ATM count (-60% vs -24%) is the classic pattern that drives deposit/recycling ATMs and unmanned self-service to absorb the closed branches' cash work: Printec's NCR intelligent-deposit/recycling ATMs, Glory/Sesami TCRs, APTRA OptiCash cash optimisation (fewer branches = longer cash cycles = more cash-holding cost) and x-core multivendor software all map directly. Sizing note: Eurobank Limited's 156 ATMs are a merged ex-Hellenic + ex-Eurobank estate, i.e. a mixed-vendor fleet that needs a single multivendor software layer.
signals.likelihood: High - merged-estate rationalisation is unavoidable during the 2026-2027 integration
signals.followup: Build an x-core + OptiCash proposal for Eurobank Limited on the explicit premise of a mixed ex-Hellenic/ex-Eurobank ATM fleet; verify the fleet's vendor mix (Hellenic historically NCR/Diebold) before pitching.

signals.signal: Post-merger integration state as of mid-2026: the legal merger completed 01/09/2025 (Hellenic Bank ceased to exist) with Eurobank S.A. becoming sole shareholder on 03/12/2025; FULL integration of digital and operational systems is stated to take two to two-and-a-half years, i.e. into 2027-2028. Fifteen branches currently run a 'branch-in-branch' model (8 ex-Eurobank + 7 ex-Hellenic) pending network integration, with significant investment stated for branch renovations and digital platforms. The bank's self-service estate is marketed as next-generation branches equipped with ATMs and 'Cash 360' machines giving 24/7 access. Group-level backdrop already in the baseline: Eurobank's ~EUR 1bn 'Banking Forward' technology programme 2025-2028.
signals.source_name: Cyprus Mail / DOM LiVE reporting on the Hellenic Bank - Eurobank Cyprus merger and integration timetable; Eurobank Cyprus 'building the bank of the future' (12/05/2026)
signals.implies: A 15-branch branch-in-branch overhang plus a stated branch-renovation budget is the single largest self-service and cash-automation refresh opportunity in Cyprus over 2026-2028. Printec entry points: NCR recycling/intelligent-deposit ATMs and Glory/Sesami TCRs to replace the duplicated 'Cash 360' deposit estate as branches consolidate, x-core multivendor ATM software over the mixed 156-ATM fleet, ATM telemetry/monitoring, 24/7 self-service zone fit-out, physical ATM security, and managed/field services through the dual-running period. Also DORA/resilience and INETCO transaction monitoring across the merged channel estate.
signals.followup: Target the 15 branch-in-branch sites first (each consolidation retires or relocates cash hardware); confirm the vendor mix of 'Cash 360' deposit machines and the ex-Hellenic ATM fleet before proposing x-core.
